subject: Temporary deviation request: night P1 on-call coverage (ClearRing)
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara@clearring.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: ops@clearring.com
Date: 2026-04-30T08:32:00-07:00
Subject: Repeated overnight P1s last week — asking about temporary SLA change

Hi Olga / Ben,

We had three P1 incidents between 01:00–04:30 PDT last week that resulted in ~25 minutes of degraded availability for our inference routes. Our engineering team traced the root cause to an autoscaling edge flakiness during a regional maintenance window; I know that Redwood's normal SLO is to respond P1 within 60 minutes 24/7.

Given our current hiring freeze and that these night incidents are recurring during the maintenance window, we want to explore a short-term operational carve-out: daytime P1 guarantees remain the same, and for nights we accept an on-call buddy model where ClearRing pagers escalate to a single on-call Redwood engineer who will triage and then call in the rotation if needed. In exchange we are asking for a small credit and a documented fallback path (cross-region failover and a named exec contact).

Can Redwood provide: 1) a temporary deviation request process we can sign, 2) the list of on-call contacts & escalation tree, and 3) a proposed credit for the three incidents?

Thanks — we want this to be short-term (4–6 weeks) but documented so our procurement/legal can sign off quickly.

Sara
Sara Patel
Head of Ops, ClearRing Inc
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara@clearring.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: marucs_lin@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-01T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Repeated overnight P1s last week — asking about temporary SLA change

Hi Sara — thanks for the detailed note and the patience. We can support a short-term, documented deviation but want to be explicit about operational implications so expectations are aligned. Draft outline below (attached I included a one-page SLA-exception-draft for legal):

- Scope: ClearRing’s P1 daytime response unchanged (60 mins), temporary night carve-out for 23:00–07:00 PDT for up to 6 weeks.
- Night model: single Redwood on-call engineer (primary) will triage P1s within 90 minutes. If unresolved or critical, the night on-call will escalate to the daytime rotation or to a named secondary (buddy) within 30 minutes of escalation.
- Fallback: automatic cross-region routing to Redwood Dedicated pool in us-west (manual trigger by ops if sustained). Expect higher tail latency during fallback.
- Credits: we propose a one-time credit equal to 2 days of platform fees prorated against last month’s usage (we'll include exact numbers).
- Escalation: named exec contact (Marcus Lin, Head of Serving) will be available for severity-1 callback during the carve-out window.
- Conditions: ClearRing to acknowledge incident postmortem within 48 hours and Redwood to provide a runbook update + 48-hour incident log deliverable.

Attached: SLA-exception-draft-20260504.pdf (editable). Also including incident log to help Ben pull exact credit numbers.

If this is acceptable we can produce a one-page amendment for signature (DocuSign) and schedule a quick alignment call.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Customer Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-02T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Repeated overnight P1s last week — asking about temporary SLA change

Quick technical note from my side (agree with the proposed deviation in principle):

- Cross-region Dedicated fallback is viable, but expect 10–25% higher median latency for affected routes due to cold cache and extra hop. That may impact ClearRing’s SLOs for latency-sensitive endpoints.
- We need a clear runbook item to force a cache warm-up (pre-warm key prefixes) when we trigger fallback; without it we will see token-cost and latency spikes for the first ~500k tokens.
- On-call buddy model is fine, but we must specify pager escalation steps in the runbook (primary → secondary within 30 minutes → Marcus (exec) as callback).

I can draft the runbook section and the warm-up playbook; Olga, can you confirm legal okay with a 4–6 week window?

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, marucs_lin@redwood.com
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-03T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Repeated overnight P1s last week — asking about temporary SLA change

Numbers and procurement side: attached is the incident-log-Apr30.csv which I pulled from our telemetry. Based on ClearRing’s last month spend, the one-time credit proposal (2 days prorated) equals $8,400 — I flagged this to finance and they are OK with a one-time credit if Legal signs the amendment limiting the window to 6 weeks.

Also recommended: include a clause that the carve-out auto-expires after 6 weeks unless both parties agree to extend. If ClearRing needs a longer runbook (and we need to add more staff), that's a separate commercial discussion.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Sara Patel <sara@clearring.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: ops@clearring.com
Date: 2026-05-04T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Repeated overnight P1s last week — asking about temporary SLA change

Thanks — this looks reasonable. We accept the 4–6 week carve-out with the night buddy model and the one-time credit ($8.4k). Two quick asks before we sign:

1) Please send the final one-page amendment (DocuSign) with precise start/end dates and the fallback latency note included.
2) Share the final on-call escalation tree with phone numbers (Marcus as exec contact is fine).

If we can get those by EOD tomorrow we can route to procurement/legal for a quick signature.

Sara
Sara Patel
Head of Ops, ClearRing Inc
